text_blocks.snippet: Occupational therapy outcome measures are tools used to assess a client's progress and the effectiveness of therapy interventions in improving occupational performance and participation. They help therapists determine a baseline, track changes, and demonstrate the value of occupational therapy.
snippet_highlighted_words: tools used to assess a client's progress and the effectiveness of therapy interventions in improving occupational performance and participation

list.snippet: COPM (Canadian Occupational Performance Measure): This client-centered measure focuses on identifying and prioritizing daily tasks that individuals struggle with, across self-care, leisure, and productivity.
TOMs (Therapy Outcome Measures): This measure assesses the severity of difficulties in areas like function, well-being, and social participation.
Visual Analog Scale (VAS): Used to measure pain intensity.
Beck Depression Inventory (BDI): Assesses the severity of depression.
Beck Anxiety Inventory (BAI): Measures the severity of anxiety.
Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS): Assesses muscle spasticity.
Goal Attainment Scaling (GAS): A personalized approach to measure goal achievement.
Functional Gait Assessment (FGA): Evaluates postural stability during walking.
Functional Mobility Tests (6MWT, TUG): Assess functional exercise capacity and mobility.

list.title: Establish Baseline:
list.snippet: Initial assessments using outcome measures help establish a starting point for therapy.

list.title: Track Progress:
list.snippet: Regular reassessments with the same measures help track changes in performance and identify areas where interventions are effective.

list.title: Demonstrate Effectiveness:
list.snippet: Outcome measures provide data to show the impact of therapy on a client's ability to participate in meaningful activities.

list.title: Inform Treatment Planning:
list.snippet: The results of outcome measures can guide therapists in adjusting interventions to best meet client needs.

list.title: Justify Services:
list.snippet: Outcome data can be used to demonstrate the value of occupational therapy to payers and stakeholders.

list.title: Improved Client Outcomes:
list.snippet: Standardized outcome measures can help therapists improve the effectiveness of their interventions.

list.title: Enhanced Communication:
list.snippet: Using standardized measures can improve communication between therapists, clients, and other healthcare professionals.

list.title: Evidence-Based Practice:
list.snippet: Outcome measures provide evidence to support the effectiveness of occupational therapy.

text_blocks.snippet: By using a variety of outcome measures, occupational therapists can ensure that their interventions are effective and tailored to the individual needs of their clients.
